# Pandamonium v1.0.58

This release completes the operator plugin experience and makes the marketplace real: installed and configured plugins are visible with click-through capability detail even without a catalog, plugin manifests can declare the configuration and API keys they need, and a signed catalog with the first shareable package can be published, installed, and updated through the existing approval lifecycle.

## MAD-940 — Plugins UI: show installed and configured plugins with capability detail

### Problem

The Add Plugins surface only rendered signed catalog packages, so with no catalog configured it showed an offline state and nothing else, and there was no way to click an installed plugin and see what it does, which tools it has, or what it needs. The ORACLE surface in the sidebar had no detail view at all. The intake flow also clipped its results (no scrolling), used the misleading "Review install" label, and offered no way back from the approval preview.

### Implementation

Adds `GET /api/extensions/installed` and `GET /api/extensions/installed/{extension_id}`: sanitized list and detail projections for registry extensions and configured surfaces (ORACLE), including capabilities with tool descriptions from the persisted inventory, permission modes, data boundaries, and configuration placeholders. The Add Plugins modal gains an **Installed** section inside the results pane that renders even while the marketplace catalog is offline, and clicking an entry opens the detail panel instead of only launching its surface. The intake flow fixes: the modal body and scan results scroll, the action is relabeled **Install plugin…** with a "nothing is installed yet" note, the approval preview scrolls into view with **Approve once** / **← Back to scan**, and the status line reports completion.

### Product value and UI visibility

Operators can now inspect everything installed on the box — including surfaces that predate the plugin registry — with the same click-through detail the marketplace offers, and the intake flow no longer strands the operator below the fold or hides the approval step.

### Verification

`tests/test_extension_plugin_view.py` (list/detail, configured surfaces, no secrets or paths), updated extension route-surface tests, `tests/browser/marketplace-installed.spec.js` (installed detail with the catalog offline), and the intake browser suite (approve-in-viewport and back control). Focused suites 17 tests, browser 6 tests, full suite green at merge.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Read-only projections; no schema, dependency, or authority change. Configured surfaces are labeled honestly and only registry installs carry manifests, inventories, and lifecycle state. Browser-surface plugin tools still need their engaged UI.

### References

- [Linear MAD-940](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-940/plugins-ui-show-installed-and-configured-plugins-with-capability)
- [Feature PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/162)

## MAD-939 — Extensions: declare required configuration and API keys in manifests

### Problem

There was no way for a plugin to declare that it needs configuration or API keys, so the operator could not see what a plugin requires before or after installing it.

### Implementation

`jos-extension.v1` gains an optional strict `configuration` array: up to 32 entries of `{key, description, required, secret}` with unique upper-snake keys, boolean flags defaulting to false, and fail-closed handling for malformed, duplicate, or unknown fields. Manifests without the field remain valid and normalize without it, so existing registry records and signed catalogs are unchanged. The installed-plugin detail projection exposes the declarations (key, description, flags) and never values; the manifest and intake runtime docs describe the contract and point values to Settings/Connections.

### Product value and UI visibility

Plugin detail now answers "what does this need to work?" — required keys are marked, secrets flagged, and the operator knows where to set them, with no secret material in any payload.

### Verification

`tests/test_extension_manifest_configuration.py` (accept/defaulting, back-compat, malformed/duplicate/unknown/bounds fail-closed), updated detail tests, full suite 5779 passed / 5 skipped.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Backward compatible by construction; declarations are metadata only and carry no values, and marketplace entries mirror the embedded manifest's declarations without overriding them.

### References

- [Linear MAD-939](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-939/extensions-declare-required-configuration-and-api-keys-in-manifests)
- [Feature PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/165)

## MAD-941 — Marketplace: publish the signed catalog with the first shareable packages

### Problem

The marketplace contract, install/update/rollback lifecycle, and discovery UI existed, but no signed catalog or package had ever been published, so Add Plugins → Available stayed offline and the marketplace could not be shared with anyone.

### Implementation

Adds `scripts/build_marketplace_catalog.py`: for each package spec it clones the pinned public ref, validates `jarvis-extension.json`, archives the exact tree, hashes and Ed25519-signs the artifact, rewrites the embedded manifest's revision to the resolved commit so entries are immutable, mirrors configuration declarations, and emits a signed `catalog.json` plus `trusted_keys.json`. Ships `marketplace/packages.json` with the ORACLE package and `docs/marketplace-publishing-runbook.md` covering key custody, build, GitHub release publication, host deployment, revocation, key rotation, rollback, and expiry. No package code is executed.

### Product value and UI visibility

The Available side of Add Plugins is now real: the signed `marketplace-v1` release carries the catalog, trusted keys, and the ORACLE 0.1.0 archive (pinned to `jos-v0.1.0`), and the operator can review and install it through the normal approval flow. Any installation can be pointed at the catalog files to see the same package list.

### Verification

`tests/test_marketplace_catalog_publish.py` (build → `validate_published_catalog` → artifact verification, tamper fail-closed, spec validation), full suite 5805 passed / 5 skipped. Live proof on CT103: catalog and keys deployed to `/srv/odysseus/data/marketplace`, host-side validation reported the ORACLE entry, and ORACLE was installed through the lifecycle (plan `4519c827`, `execute_plan` succeeded, enabled at pinned revision `b619e2a17015` with a populated 12+ capability inventory).

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

The signing private key lives outside Git (`~/.config/pandamonium/marketplace-signing.pem`, key id `pandamonium-marketplace-2026`); only the public half is deployed. Catalog entries must reference immutable revisions, and catalogs expire (default 90 days), failing closed until rotated. The first tranche is ORACLE; additional maintained forks and the cybersecurity tranche follow separately.
